angle: 30 money rules for 2027: numbers, psychology, action
title: 30 Money Rules to Live By in 2027

scenes.text: Hi, I'm Ryan Rover. A new year is coming, and with it, a fresh start for your money. But instead of vague resolutions that fade by February, I want to give you something better: thirty simple money rules to live by in 2027. Rules you can remember, rules you can follow, and rules that work whether you earn thirty thousand dollars or three hundred thousand.
scenes.caption: RYAN
scenes.chapter: Intro

scenes.text: Why rules instead of goals? Because goals tell you where you want to go, but rules tell you what to do every day. Rules remove decisions. When you already know your rule, you don't have to think about it in the moment, when emotions are high and willpower is low.
scenes.caption: RULES REMOVE DECISIONS
scenes.short_hook: 30 money rules to live by in 2027

scenes.text: We'll go through these thirty rules in three groups, three angles. First, ten rules about the numbers: the targets and ratios that keep your finances healthy. Second, ten rules about the psychology: how to think and behave with money. And third, ten action rules: the playbook of habits that protect and grow what you have.
scenes.caption: THREE ANGLES, 30 RULES

scenes.text: Stay for rule fifteen. It could protect you from one of the fastest growing threats to your money. Let's start with the numbers.
scenes.caption: RYAN

scenes.text: Every January, millions of people make financial resolutions. Save more. Spend less. Pay off debt. And by spring, many have quietly given up. The problem isn't motivation. It's that resolutions are vague, and vague goals give your brain nothing specific to do.
scenes.caption: RESOLUTIONS FADE
scenes.chapter: Why rules beat resolutions

scenes.text: Psychologists call specific plans implementation intentions. Research by psychologist Peter Gollwitzer and others found that people who decide in advance exactly what they'll do in a specific situation are more likely to follow through. When X happens, I do Y. Money rules work the same way.
scenes.caption: WHEN X, I DO Y

scenes.text: When a raise arrives, half goes to savings. When I want something over one hundred dollars, I wait forty eight hours. When the market drops, I keep investing. Each rule is a decision made once, calmly, that protects you in hundreds of future moments.
scenes.caption: DECIDE ONCE

scenes.text: Guidelines in this video come from widely used sources, including the Federal Reserve, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Federal Trade Commission, the IRS and Fidelity. Growth examples are stated math and are illustrations, not promises. These rules are general guidelines, not personal advice, and your situation may call for different numbers.
scenes.caption: OUR SOURCES
scenes.chapter: How we got the numbers

scenes.text: Angle one. Ten rules about the numbers.
scenes.caption: RYAN
scenes.chapter: Angle 1: The Numbers

scenes.text: Rule 1. Keep 3 to 6 months of essentials in cash.

card.title: Keep 3 to 6 months of essentials in cash

scenes.caption: RULE 1
scenes.chapter: Rule 1. Keep 3 to 6 months of essentials in cash

scenes.text: Rule one. Keep three to six months of essential expenses in a high yield savings account. In recent Federal Reserve surveys, more than a third of American adults said they couldn't cover a four hundred dollar emergency with cash. An emergency fund is what keeps surprises from becoming debt.
scenes.caption: 3 TO 6 MONTHS

scenes.text: If you're starting from zero, start with five hundred dollars, then one thousand, then one month. Every stage protects you more than the last. In 2027, make this your first priority if you don't have it yet.
scenes.caption: START WITH $500

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: open a separate high yield savings account if you don't have one, name it Emergency Fund, and set an automatic transfer for the day after payday. Then put a share of your tax refund in it this spring. Those two moves alone can get many people to their first thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: 2027: OPEN, AUTOMATE, REFUND

scenes.text: Rule 2. Save at least 15% for retirement.

card.title: Save at least 15% for retirement

scenes.caption: RULE 2
scenes.chapter: Rule 2. Save at least 15% for retirement

scenes.text: Rule two. Save at least fifteen percent of your gross income for retirement, including any employer match. It's one of the most common guidelines from retirement planners. If you start late, aim higher.
scenes.caption: 15% OR MORE

scenes.text: If fifteen percent isn't possible yet, raise your contribution by one percent every few months. Many workplace plans offer automatic increases. Turn them on, and in a couple of years you'll get there without feeling a sudden pinch.
scenes.caption: ONE PERCENT AT A TIME

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: log into your retirement plan in January and write down your current contribution rate. If it's below fifteen percent, raise it by at least one or two points now, and schedule another increase for July. If you get a raise this year, send half of it to your retirement contribution.
scenes.caption: 2027: RAISE IT IN JANUARY

scenes.text: Rule 3. Never leave the match on the table.

card.title: Never leave the match on the table

scenes.caption: RULE 3
scenes.chapter: Rule 3. Never leave the match on the table

scenes.text: Rule three. If your employer matches retirement contributions, always contribute enough to get the full match. On a sixty thousand dollar salary, a four percent match is twenty four hundred dollars a year. Not taking it is turning down a raise.
scenes.caption: FREE MONEY

scenes.text: Check your plan's match formula and vesting schedule this month. If you're not getting the full match, fixing it might be the single highest return move you make all year.
scenes.caption: CHECK IT THIS MONTH

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: if you change jobs this year, ask about the match during the offer process, and enroll on day one. Some employers have waiting periods or require you to opt in. Don't let months of free money slip by because of paperwork.
scenes.caption: 2027: ENROLL ON DAY ONE

scenes.text: Rule 4. Pay off any debt above about 8%.

card.title: Pay off any debt above about 8%

scenes.caption: RULE 4
scenes.chapter: Rule 4. Pay off any debt above about 8%

scenes.text: Rule four. Treat debt above roughly eight percent interest as an emergency. Credit card rates have often averaged above twenty percent in recent years, according to Federal Reserve data. Paying off a twenty two percent card is like earning a guaranteed twenty two percent return.
scenes.caption: ABOVE 8% = PRIORITY

scenes.text: List your debts by interest rate, pay minimums on all of them, and attack the highest rate first. When one is gone, roll its payment into the next.
scenes.caption: HIGHEST RATE FIRST

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: write every debt on one page with its balance, rate and minimum payment. Circle the highest rate. That's your target for the year. Set an automatic extra payment toward it, even fifty dollars a month, and add any windfalls.
scenes.caption: 2027: CIRCLE THE TARGET

scenes.text: Rule 5. Keep housing around 30% of gross income or less.

card.title: Keep housing around 30% of gross income or less

scenes.caption: RULE 5
scenes.chapter: Rule 5. Keep housing around 30% of gross income or less

scenes.text: Rule five. A common guideline is to keep housing costs at or below about thirty percent of gross income. Housing is usually the largest expense in any budget, around a third of household spending in BLS data. Getting this one decision right makes every other goal easier.
scenes.caption: ~30% OR LESS

scenes.text: In expensive cities, that may not be possible right away. If so, look for ways to bring it down over time: a roommate, a cheaper unit at renewal, or a smaller home. Every hundred dollars saved on housing is twelve hundred a year.
scenes.caption: BRING IT DOWN OVER TIME

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: if your lease is up this year, compare at least three alternatives before renewing, and use them to negotiate. If you own, check whether your property taxes and insurance have risen and shop your homeowners policy. Small housing savings repeat every single month.
scenes.caption: 2027: SHOP BEFORE RENEWING

scenes.text: Rule 6. Use the rule of 72.

card.title: Use the rule of 72

scenes.caption: RULE 6
scenes.chapter: Rule 6. Use the rule of 72

scenes.text: Rule six. Divide seventy two by an interest rate to estimate how many years it takes money to double. At seven percent, money doubles in about ten years. At ten percent, about seven years.
scenes.caption: 72 ÷ RATE = YEARS TO DOUBLE

scenes.text: It works for debt too. At twenty two percent credit card interest, an unpaid balance can roughly double in about three and a half years if interest keeps compounding. Knowing this one number helps you understand both sides of compounding.
scenes.caption: IT WORKS FOR DEBT TOO

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: use the rule of seventy two on your own accounts. What rate is your savings account earning, and how long until it doubles? What rate is your credit card charging? Seeing those two numbers side by side is often the push people need to move money to the right place.
scenes.caption: 2027: RUN YOUR NUMBERS

scenes.text: Rule 7. Keep investment fees as low as possible.

card.title: Keep investment fees as low as possible

scenes.caption: RULE 7
scenes.chapter: Rule 7. Keep investment fees as low as possible

scenes.text: Rule seven. Pay attention to the expense ratio, the yearly fee on a fund. Many broad index funds charge well under a quarter of a percent. Some actively managed funds charge one percent or more.
scenes.caption: WATCH THE EXPENSE RATIO

scenes.text: The difference adds up. Investing five hundred dollars a month for thirty years, a six percent net return could grow to about five hundred two thousand dollars. A five percent net return, the same investment with one percent more in fees, about four hundred sixteen thousand. That one percent costs roughly eighty six thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: 1% IN FEES = ~$86K

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: look up the expense ratio of every fund you own. It's listed on your account website or the fund's page. If any fund charges much more than a comparable index fund, consider whether it's worth it. Check for account fees too, like advisory fees or maintenance charges.
scenes.caption: 2027: LOOK UP YOUR FEES

scenes.text: Five hundred dollars a month for thirty years, at a six percent net return versus five percent after an extra one percent in fees.
Rule 8. Keep total car costs under control.

card.title: Keep total car costs under control
card.sub: cars are the quiet wealth killer

scenes.caption: RULE 8
scenes.chapter: Rule 8. Keep total car costs under control

scenes.text: Rule eight. A popular guideline is the twenty four ten rule: put at least twenty percent down, finance for no more than four years, and keep total car costs, including payment, insurance and gas, under ten percent of gross income. Many people use a looser version, but the idea is the same.
scenes.caption: THE 20/4/10 RULE

scenes.text: Cars lose value quickly, especially in the first few years. Buying a reliable used car and keeping it for a long time is one of the most consistent wealth building habits there is.
scenes.caption: BUY RELIABLE, KEEP IT LONG

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: if your car is paid off and reliable, keep driving it and send the old payment amount to savings. If you need a car, set a total budget before you shop, get financing quotes from a credit union before visiting the dealer, and focus on the total price, not the monthly payment.
scenes.caption: 2027: TOTAL PRICE, NOT PAYMENT

scenes.text: Rule 9. Know your number: 25 times spending.

card.title: Know your number: 25 times spending

scenes.caption: RULE 9
scenes.chapter: Rule 9. Know your number: 25 times spending

scenes.text: Rule nine. Know roughly how much you need to be financially independent. Based on the four percent rule from William Bengen's 1994 research, a common estimate is twenty five times your yearly spending. Spend forty thousand a year, and your number is about one million dollars.
scenes.caption: SPENDING × 25

scenes.text: It's a rough guideline, and early retirees often use a more cautious multiple. But knowing your number turns retirement from a vague worry into a concrete target.
scenes.caption: A CONCRETE TARGET

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: add up your spending for 2026, multiply by twenty five, and write the number down. Then compare it with what you have invested today. The gap tells you how far you have to go, and the savings rate table can tell you roughly how long it will take.
scenes.caption: 2027: WRITE YOUR NUMBER

scenes.text: Rule 10. Check your net worth once a year.

card.title: Check your net worth once a year

scenes.caption: RULE 10
scenes.chapter: Rule 10. Check your net worth once a year

scenes.text: Rule ten. Once a year, add up what you own and subtract what you owe. That's your net worth, the single best measure of financial progress. Fidelity suggests rough retirement savings targets of about one times your salary by thirty, three times by forty, and six times by fifty.
scenes.caption: ONCE A YEAR

scenes.text: Don't panic if you're behind. Watch the direction. A net worth that rises every year, even slowly, means your plan is working.
scenes.caption: WATCH THE DIRECTION

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: pick a date, like New Year's Day or your birthday, and calculate your net worth every year on that date. Keep a simple list going back year after year. Over a decade, that list becomes one of the most motivating documents you own.
scenes.caption: 2027: PICK A DATE

scenes.text: Angle two. Ten rules about how to think and behave with money.
scenes.caption: RYAN
scenes.chapter: Angle 2: The Psychology

scenes.text: Rule 11. Pay yourself first.

card.title: Pay yourself first
card.sub: the future gets paid before the present

scenes.caption: RULE 11
scenes.chapter: Rule 11. Pay yourself first
scenes.short_hook: 10 money mindset rules that change everything

scenes.text: Rule eleven. Before you pay for anything else, pay your future. Set up automatic transfers to savings and investing on payday. What's left is yours to spend. This flips the usual order, where people save whatever happens to be left over, which is often nothing.
scenes.caption: FUTURE FIRST

scenes.text: This rule works because it doesn't rely on discipline. Once it's set, it happens whether you're motivated or not.
scenes.caption: NO DISCIPLINE REQUIRED

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: set up your transfers so they happen the same day your pay arrives, and give each one a clear job: emergency fund, investing, sinking funds. Then forget about them. Check once a month that they ran.
scenes.caption: 2027: SAME DAY AS PAYDAY

scenes.text: Rule 12. Spend extravagantly on what you love, cut mercilessly on what you don't.

card.title: Spend extravagantly on what you love, cut mercilessly on what you don't

scenes.caption: RULE 12
scenes.chapter: Rule 12. Spend extravagantly on what you love, cut mercilessly on what you don't

scenes.text: Rule twelve. This idea, popularized by author Ramit Sethi, is called conscious spending. Identify the two or three things that bring you real joy, and spend on them without guilt. Then cut costs ruthlessly everywhere else.
scenes.caption: LOVE IT OR CUT IT

scenes.text: This is how people save a lot without feeling deprived. They aren't spending less on everything. They're spending more on what matters and nothing on what doesn't.
scenes.caption: NOT DEPRIVED

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: write down your three favorite ways to spend money, the ones that truly make your life better. Then look at your last three months of spending and circle everything that didn't make you happier. That's where your cuts come from, painlessly.
scenes.caption: 2027: NAME YOUR THREE

scenes.text: Rule 13. Wait 48 hours before big purchases.

card.title: Wait 48 hours before big purchases

scenes.caption: RULE 13
scenes.chapter: Rule 13. Wait 48 hours before big purchases

scenes.text: Rule thirteen. For any non essential purchase above a set amount, say one hundred dollars, wait forty eight hours. For very large purchases, wait thirty days. Many impulse urges fade once the moment passes.
scenes.caption: 48 HOURS

scenes.text: Remove saved cards from shopping apps and unsubscribe from sale emails. Adding a little friction gives your rational brain time to catch up with your emotional brain.
scenes.caption: ADD FRICTION

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: keep a wish list. When you want something, add it to the list with the date and price. Review the list every couple of weeks. Many people find that most items no longer feel important, and the few that remain are the ones truly worth buying.
scenes.caption: 2027: KEEP A WISH LIST

scenes.text: Rule 14. Don't compare your finances to social media.

card.title: Don't compare your finances to social media

scenes.caption: RULE 14
scenes.chapter: Rule 14. Don't compare your finances to social media

scenes.text: Rule fourteen. Online, you see vacations, new cars and renovations. You don't see the credit card statements, the loans, or the stress. Comparing your behind the scenes with someone else's highlight reel will make you feel poor and push you to overspend.
scenes.caption: HIGHLIGHTS ONLY

scenes.text: Measure your progress against your own past. Is your savings rate higher than last year? Is your debt lower? That's the only comparison that matters.
scenes.caption: YOU VS. YOU

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: unfollow accounts that make you feel you need to buy things, and follow a few that teach you about money. Your feed shapes your wants more than you think. Change the feed, and you change the wants.
scenes.caption: 2027: CHANGE YOUR FEED

scenes.text: Rule 15. If it sounds too good to be true, it is.

card.title: If it sounds too good to be true, it is

scenes.caption: RULE 15
scenes.chapter: Rule 15. If it sounds too good to be true, it is

scenes.text: Rule fifteen. According to the Federal Trade Commission, consumers reported losing more than twelve billion dollars to fraud in 2024, and investment scams were the largest category of losses. Scammers use fake investment platforms, romance scams, impersonation of banks and government agencies, and promises of guaranteed returns.
scenes.caption: $12 BILLION+ LOST TO FRAUD

scenes.text: Protect yourself with simple rules. No legitimate investment guarantees high returns with no risk. Never send money to someone you've only met online. Never pay with gift cards or crypto because someone says it's urgent. And when in doubt, hang up and call the official number yourself.
scenes.caption: HANG UP AND VERIFY

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: talk to older family members about scams, since criminals often target them. Agree on a family code word for emergencies, so a fake call claiming a relative is in trouble can be checked. And set up account alerts for large transactions on every bank and card account.
scenes.caption: 2027: A FAMILY CODE WORD

scenes.text: Rule 16. Time in the market beats timing the market.

card.title: Time in the market beats timing the market

scenes.caption: RULE 16
scenes.chapter: Rule 16. Time in the market beats timing the market

scenes.text: Rule sixteen. Trying to jump in and out of the market to avoid drops usually backfires. Some of the market's best days have historically come shortly after its worst days. Investors who sell in a panic often miss the recovery.
scenes.caption: STAY INVESTED

scenes.text: Invest regularly, in good markets and bad. When prices fall, your regular contributions simply buy more shares.
scenes.caption: KEEP BUYING

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: write down your plan for the next market drop before it happens. For example: when the market falls twenty percent, I keep my contributions the same and do not sell. Having it in writing makes it much easier to follow when headlines get scary.
scenes.caption: 2027: WRITE YOUR DROP PLAN

scenes.text: Rule 17. Never invest in what you can't explain.

card.title: Never invest in what you can't explain

scenes.caption: RULE 17
scenes.chapter: Rule 17. Never invest in what you can't explain

scenes.text: Rule seventeen. If you can't explain how an investment makes money in two sentences, don't buy it. Complexity often hides high fees, high risk, or both.
scenes.caption: EXPLAIN IT IN 2 SENTENCES

scenes.text: Broad index funds are easy to explain: you own a small piece of many companies, and you share in their growth. That simplicity is a feature, not a weakness.
scenes.caption: SIMPLE IS A FEATURE

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: if someone pitches you an investment, ask three questions. How does it make money? What are all the fees? What happens if I need my money back? If the answers are vague or pressured, walk away.
scenes.caption: 2027: ASK THREE QUESTIONS

scenes.text: Rule 18. Automate every good decision.

card.title: Automate every good decision

scenes.caption: RULE 18
scenes.chapter: Rule 18. Automate every good decision

scenes.text: Rule eighteen. Automate savings, investing, bill payments, and contribution increases. Every decision you automate is one you never have to make again when you're tired, busy or tempted.
scenes.caption: SYSTEMS BEAT WILLPOWER

scenes.text: Researchers Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi showed with their Save More Tomorrow program that automatic, pre committed increases helped workers raise their savings rates dramatically. Automation works with human nature, not against it.
scenes.caption: IT WORKS WITH HUMAN NATURE

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: make a list of every money task you still do manually, like transferring savings, paying bills or investing. Automate one per week for the next month. By February, your money will mostly run itself.
scenes.caption: 2027: ONE PER WEEK

scenes.text: Rule 19. Let your lifestyle rise slower than your income.

card.title: Let your lifestyle rise slower than your income

scenes.caption: RULE 19
scenes.chapter: Rule 19. Let your lifestyle rise slower than your income

scenes.text: Rule nineteen. When you get a raise, send at least half of it to savings and investing. Enjoy the other half. Your life still improves, but your savings rate climbs every year.
scenes.caption: HALF OF EVERY RAISE

scenes.text: Lifestyle creep is how people with good incomes stay stuck. Each upgrade feels small, but together they lock in high fixed costs. This rule keeps you moving forward.
scenes.caption: AVOID THE CREEP

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: before your next raise arrives, decide exactly how much will go to savings and how much to your lifestyle. Write it down. Once the money hits your account, it's much harder to decide calmly.
scenes.caption: 2027: DECIDE BEFORE IT ARRIVES

scenes.text: Rule 20. Money is a tool, not a scoreboard.

card.title: Money is a tool, not a scoreboard
card.sub: use it for a good life

scenes.caption: RULE 20
scenes.chapter: Rule 20. Money is a tool, not a scoreboard

scenes.text: Rule twenty. The goal isn't the biggest number. It's a life with security, freedom and meaning. Use money to buy time, experiences, health and peace of mind.
scenes.caption: A TOOL FOR A GOOD LIFE

scenes.text: Research by psychologists including Elizabeth Dunn has suggested that spending on experiences, on others, and on buying back time can increase happiness more than spending on more stuff. Keep that in mind when you plan your spending.
scenes.caption: EXPERIENCES AND TIME

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: plan one experience you'll pay for in cash this year, something that truly matters to you. A trip, a class, a family event. Put it in a sinking fund. Money becomes much more meaningful when it's connected to the life you want.
scenes.caption: 2027: PLAN ONE EXPERIENCE

scenes.text: Quick pause. If these rules are useful, subscribe to the channel. It's free, and it helps me keep making these videos for you all year. Now, the last ten. The action rules.
scenes.caption: RYAN
scenes.chapter: A quick favor

scenes.text: Angle three. Ten action rules. The habits that protect and grow your money.
scenes.caption: RYAN
scenes.chapter: Angle 3: The Playbook

scenes.text: Rule 21. Check your credit reports regularly.

card.title: Check your credit reports regularly

scenes.caption: RULE 21
scenes.chapter: Rule 21. Check your credit reports regularly

scenes.text: Rule twenty one. You can check your credit reports from the three major bureaus for free at annualcreditreport dot com, the official site. Look for accounts you don't recognize and errors in your payment history.
scenes.caption: FREE REPORTS

scenes.text: Errors happen, and they can raise your borrowing costs. Disputing them is free. And unfamiliar accounts can be an early warning of identity theft.
scenes.caption: DISPUTE ERRORS

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: put a reminder in your calendar to check one bureau every four months, or all three at once a couple of times a year. It takes about fifteen minutes and costs nothing.
scenes.caption: 2027: SET A REMINDER

scenes.text: Rule 22. Freeze your credit.

card.title: Freeze your credit

scenes.caption: RULE 22
scenes.chapter: Rule 22. Freeze your credit

scenes.text: Rule twenty two. A credit freeze stops new lenders from accessing your credit report, which makes it much harder for criminals to open accounts in your name. Under federal law, freezing and unfreezing your credit with each bureau is free.
scenes.caption: FREEZE IS FREE

scenes.text: You can temporarily lift the freeze when you apply for a loan or a new card. It takes a few minutes online, and it's one of the best protections available.
scenes.caption: LIFT IT WHEN NEEDED

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: freeze your credit at all three major bureaus this month. Save the logins or PINs somewhere secure. Consider doing the same for your children, since child identity theft can go undetected for years.
scenes.caption: 2027: ALL THREE BUREAUS

scenes.text: Rule 23. Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience.

card.title: Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience

scenes.caption: RULE 23
scenes.chapter: Rule 23. Insure against catastrophe, not inconvenience

scenes.text: Rule twenty three. Insurance is for events that would wreck your finances: serious illness, disability, death of an earner, a house fire, a major lawsuit. Make sure those are covered with health, disability, term life if others depend on you, home or renters, and adequate liability coverage.
scenes.caption: COVER THE CATASTROPHES

scenes.text: For small risks, like a phone screen or a minor car dent, extended warranties and low deductibles often cost more than they're worth. Your emergency fund can cover those.
scenes.caption: SKIP THE SMALL STUFF

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: review each insurance policy once this year. Is your deductible right for your emergency fund? Is your liability coverage enough? Do you still need every add on? Many people find savings and gaps at the same time.
scenes.caption: 2027: REVIEW EACH POLICY

scenes.text: Rule 24. Name your beneficiaries and have a will.

card.title: Name your beneficiaries and have a will

scenes.caption: RULE 24
scenes.chapter: Rule 24. Name your beneficiaries and have a will

scenes.text: Rule twenty four. Make sure every retirement account and life insurance policy has up to date beneficiaries. In many cases, beneficiary designations can override what a will says.
scenes.caption: UPDATE BENEFICIARIES

scenes.text: And have at least a basic will, especially if you have children. It's one of the kindest things you can do for your family, and it often costs far less than people expect.
scenes.caption: HAVE A WILL

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: log into every account with a beneficiary option, including retirement plans, IRAs, life insurance and bank accounts that allow payable on death designations. Make sure the names are current. Life changes like marriage, divorce and new children are the most common reasons they go out of date.
scenes.caption: 2027: CHECK EVERY ACCOUNT

scenes.text: Rule 25. Always negotiate.

card.title: Always negotiate

scenes.caption: RULE 25
scenes.chapter: Rule 25. Always negotiate

scenes.text: Rule twenty five. Negotiate your salary, your rent renewal, your insurance, your internet bill, and large purchases. Not every negotiation works, but asking politely costs nothing.
scenes.caption: ASK

scenes.text: Salary matters most. A raise compounds into future raises and retirement contributions for the rest of your career. Research typical pay for your role, bring evidence of your results, and ask.
scenes.caption: SALARY FIRST

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: pick three bills to negotiate in the first quarter: for example internet, phone and car insurance. Call, ask for a better rate or a loyalty discount, and mention competitor prices. Even one success can save hundreds over the year.
scenes.caption: 2027: THREE CALLS

scenes.text: Rule 26. Use tax advantaged accounts first.

card.title: Use tax advantaged accounts first

scenes.caption: RULE 26
scenes.chapter: Rule 26. Use tax advantaged accounts first

scenes.text: Rule twenty six. Before investing in a regular brokerage account, use tax advantaged accounts: your workplace plan, an IRA, and a health savings account if you qualify. Check the IRS website for the 2027 contribution limits, since they're adjusted for inflation.
scenes.caption: TAX ADVANTAGES FIRST

scenes.text: Over decades, the tax savings can add up to tens of thousands of dollars or more. It's one of the simplest ways to make your money grow faster without taking more risk.
scenes.caption: GROW FASTER, SAME RISK

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: if you're eligible for an IRA, consider contributing early in the year rather than at the deadline, so your money has more time to grow. And if you have a high deductible health plan, check whether you're using your health savings account fully.
scenes.caption: 2027: CONTRIBUTE EARLY

scenes.text: Rule 27. Review subscriptions twice a year.

card.title: Review subscriptions twice a year

scenes.caption: RULE 27
scenes.chapter: Rule 27. Review subscriptions twice a year

scenes.text: Rule twenty seven. In a 2022 survey by C plus R Research, people underestimated their monthly subscription spending by more than half. Twice a year, list every recurring charge and cancel what you don't use.
scenes.caption: TWICE A YEAR

scenes.text: Put the reviews on your calendar, for example in January and July. And rotate streaming services instead of keeping them all at once.
scenes.caption: JANUARY AND JULY

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: when you sign up for a free trial, set a calendar reminder for the day before it ends. Many subscriptions start as free trials that people simply forget to cancel.
scenes.caption: 2027: TRIAL REMINDERS

scenes.text: Rule 28. Build sinking funds for predictable costs.

card.title: Build sinking funds for predictable costs

scenes.caption: RULE 28
scenes.chapter: Rule 28. Build sinking funds for predictable costs

scenes.text: Rule twenty eight. Car repairs, holidays, birthdays and annual bills aren't emergencies. They're predictable, just irregular. Set aside a small amount every month in separate savings buckets for each one.
scenes.caption: PLAN THE IRREGULAR

scenes.text: Sinking funds protect your emergency fund and your budget. When the bill arrives, the money is already there.
scenes.caption: THE MONEY IS WAITING

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: list every irregular expense you had in 2026. Add them up and divide by twelve. That's your monthly sinking fund total. Set it up as an automatic transfer and split it into buckets.
scenes.caption: 2027: LIST LAST YEAR'S

scenes.text: Rule 29. Talk about money with the people you share life with.

card.title: Talk about money with the people you share life with

scenes.caption: RULE 29
scenes.chapter: Rule 29. Talk about money with the people you share life with

scenes.text: Rule twenty nine. If you have a partner, talk about money regularly: goals, debts, spending, and fears. Money is one of the most commonly reported sources of stress in relationships. Regular, calm conversations prevent bigger conflicts later.
scenes.caption: TALK REGULARLY

scenes.text: Try a monthly money date: thirty minutes, a quick review, and one decision for the month ahead. End it with something fun.
scenes.caption: A MONTHLY MONEY DATE

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: schedule your first money date in January. Bring three things: a list of accounts and balances, your top goal for the year, and one thing you'd love to spend on. Start with goals, not blame.
scenes.caption: 2027: FIRST DATE IN JANUARY

scenes.text: Rule 30. Invest in yourself every year.

card.title: Invest in yourself every year

scenes.caption: RULE 30
scenes.chapter: Rule 30. Invest in yourself every year

scenes.text: Rule thirty. For most people, their ability to earn is their biggest financial asset. Every year, invest in it: a new skill, a certification, a course, better health, or stronger relationships in your field.
scenes.caption: YOUR BIGGEST ASSET

scenes.text: A skill that raises your income by even a few thousand dollars a year can be worth more than almost any investment decision. And unlike the market, it's something you control.
scenes.caption: SOMETHING YOU CONTROL

scenes.text: How to apply it in 2027: choose one skill that would make you more valuable at work and commit to learning it this year. Ask your employer about training budgets or tuition help. Many companies offer them, and many employees never use them.
scenes.caption: 2027: ONE SKILL THIS YEAR

scenes.text: Notice how the action rules work together. Checking your reports, freezing your credit and naming beneficiaries protect what you have. Negotiating, tax advantages and investing in yourself grow it. Sinking funds, subscription reviews and money conversations keep the whole system running smoothly. None of them takes long. Together, they make your finances far more resilient.
scenes.caption: THEY WORK TOGETHER

scenes.text: Here's a simple way to roll these rules out over the year. January: rules two, eleven and eighteen. Raise your retirement contribution, pay yourself first, and automate. February: rules twenty one and twenty two. Check and freeze your credit. March: rules four and twenty five. Target your highest rate debt and negotiate three bills.
scenes.caption: JANUARY TO MARCH
scenes.chapter: A month by month plan for 2027

scenes.text: April: rule one, using your tax refund to build your emergency fund. May: rules seven and twenty six, fees and tax advantaged accounts. June: rules twenty three and twenty four, insurance and beneficiaries. July: rule twenty seven, the mid year subscription review.
scenes.caption: APRIL TO JULY

scenes.text: August: rule twenty eight, sinking funds for the holidays. September: rule thirty, pick a skill. October: rule sixteen, write your market drop plan. November: rule twelve, plan spending you love for the holidays. And December: rules nine and ten, your number and your net worth. By the end of the year, all thirty rules are part of your life.
scenes.caption: AUGUST TO DECEMBER

scenes.text: Let's imagine one person following these rules for a year. Carmen earns fifty eight thousand dollars and starts 2027 with about eight hundred dollars in savings, a three thousand dollar credit card balance, and a five percent retirement contribution with a five percent match she wasn't fully getting.
scenes.caption: CARMEN IN JANUARY
scenes.chapter: What a year of rules can do
scenes.short_hook: What one year of following money rules can do

scenes.text: In January, she raises her contribution to get the full match and automates everything. In March, she negotiates her internet and insurance, saving about sixty dollars a month. In April, she puts most of her tax refund toward the card. By summer, the card is gone, and its payment flows into her emergency fund.
scenes.caption: CARMEN BY SUMMER

scenes.text: By December, Carmen has about four thousand dollars in her emergency fund, no credit card debt, a higher retirement balance, frozen credit, updated beneficiaries, and a clear yearly net worth number. Nothing dramatic happened. She just followed a handful of rules, month after month.
scenes.caption: CARMEN IN DECEMBER

scenes.text: This is an illustration, not a promise. But it shows how simple rules, applied consistently, can change a financial life in a single year. And the second year is usually easier than the first, because the systems are already in place.
scenes.caption: YEAR TWO IS EASIER

scenes.text: Question one. Which rule matters most? If you only follow one, make it rule eleven, pay yourself first, with automation. It quietly powers most of the others.
scenes.caption: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE
scenes.chapter: Questions people ask

scenes.text: Question two. What if I can't follow a rule because of my situation? That's fine. These are guidelines, not laws. If your housing is above thirty percent or you can't save fifteen percent yet, focus on moving in the right direction. Progress beats perfection.
scenes.caption: PROGRESS BEATS PERFECTION

scenes.text: Question three. What if my partner doesn't want to follow these rules? Start with the ones you can do on your own, like your own retirement contribution, your credit freeze and your subscriptions. Share results, not lectures. When a partner sees the emergency fund grow or a debt disappear, they're often more willing to join in.
scenes.caption: A PARTNER WHO ISN'T ON BOARD

scenes.text: Question four. How do I remember all thirty? You don't need to. Print the list, or save it on your phone, and review it once a month during your money check. Over time, the rules you use most become automatic, and you'll only need the list for the rest.
scenes.caption: HOW TO REMEMBER THEM

scenes.text: And question five. Are these rules different for 2027 than for any other year? Mostly not. Good money rules are timeless. What changes each year are the details: contribution limits, interest rates, tax rules, and new types of scams. Check the official sources each year for the latest numbers.
scenes.caption: TIMELESS RULES

scenes.text: Let's recap all thirty. The numbers. One: three to six months of essentials in cash. Two: save fifteen percent for retirement. Three: never leave the match on the table. Four: pay off debt above about eight percent. Five: housing around thirty percent or less.
scenes.caption: RULES 1 TO 5
scenes.chapter: Recap: all 30 rules

scenes.text: Six: use the rule of seventy two. Seven: keep investment fees low. Eight: keep car costs under control. Nine: know your number, twenty five times spending. Ten: check your net worth once a year.
scenes.caption: RULES 6 TO 10

scenes.text: The psychology. Eleven: pay yourself first. Twelve: spend on what you love, cut what you don't. Thirteen: wait forty eight hours. Fourteen: don't compare to social media. Fifteen: if it sounds too good to be true, it is.
scenes.caption: RULES 11 TO 15

scenes.text: Sixteen: time in the market beats timing. Seventeen: never invest in what you can't explain. Eighteen: automate every good decision. Nineteen: let lifestyle rise slower than income. Twenty: money is a tool, not a scoreboard.
scenes.caption: RULES 16 TO 20

scenes.text: The action rules. Twenty one: check your credit reports. Twenty two: freeze your credit. Twenty three: insure against catastrophe. Twenty four: name beneficiaries and have a will. Twenty five: always negotiate.
scenes.caption: RULES 21 TO 25

scenes.text: Twenty six: use tax advantaged accounts first. Twenty seven: review subscriptions twice a year. Twenty eight: build sinking funds. Twenty nine: talk about money with your partner. And thirty: invest in yourself every year.
scenes.caption: RULES 26 TO 30

scenes.text: One last thought. Rules can sound restrictive, but these thirty do the opposite. They free you from having to make the same hard decisions again and again. They protect you from scams, debt and panic. And they leave you with more money, more time and more choices. That's what a good year with money really looks like. Here's to making 2027 that year, for you and the people you love.
scenes.caption: HERE'S TO 2027

scenes.text: And if you only remember three rules from today, remember these. Pay yourself first. Never leave the match on the table. And if it sounds too good to be true, it is.
scenes.caption: IF YOU REMEMBER THREE

scenes.text: You don't need to follow all thirty at once. Pick three for January, three for February, and so on. By the end of 2027, you'll have built a money system most people never do. And watch my final video in this series: the complete playbook from broke to one million dollars. I'm Ryan Rover. See you in the next one.
scenes.caption: RYAN
